extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, legislators, and political thinkers concerned with constitution-making
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical and practical critique of constitutional design and the temperament/method of lawgivers, using the French Revolution's Assembly as a case study. Focuses on principles for framing representative government and cautions against abstract or destructive reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront difficulty rather than evade it
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulty should be confronted and overcome; evading difficulty leads to superficial solutions and arbitrary power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "purpose everywhere seems to have been to evade and slip aside from _difficulty_. This it has been the glory of the great masters in all the arts to confront, and to overcome...Difficulty is a severe instructor...He that wrestles with us strengthens our nerves and sharpens our skill." Anti-pattern: starting reforms from 'sloth' or seeking short-cuts which create feeble, vicious, and insecure results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer gradual preservation-and-reform over wholesale destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective reform preserves useful parts of old establishments and fits new additions to what is retained by slow, deliberate work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "At once to preserve and to reform is quite another thing...a vigorous mind, steady, persevering attention...are to be exercised." Anti-pattern: commencing reform with abolition and total destruction — mobs can destroy but not build; slow, time-assisted progress allows observation and correction ('from light to light').

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawgivers should possess sensibility, humility, and deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: The true lawgiver ought to have a heart full of sensibility, to love and respect mankind, to fear himself, and to move deliberately even if he apprehends the ultimate object intuitively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The true lawgiver ought to have a heart full of sensibility...He ought to love and respect his kind, and to fear himself...his movements towards it ought to be deliberate." Implies moral temperament matters as much as intellect in framing laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political arrangement must be achieved by social (consultative) means
rubrics_metrics.description: Because politics concerns social ends, it must be worked by social means — minds must conspire with mind; time and experience are required to produce the consensus needed for durable arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Political arrangement, as it is a work for social ends, is to be only wrought by social means. There mind must conspire with mind. Time is required..." Encourages consultation, involving many minds and generations; experience improves plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experience and multiple perspectives to amend designs
rubrics_metrics.description: No plan should be final without observation and amendment by those of lesser or differing abilities; experience and the input of many improve and correct initial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "I have never yet seen any plan which has not been mended by the observations of those who were much inferior in understanding to the person who took the lead...By a slow, but well-sustained progress, the effect of each step is watched." Emphasizes iterative pilot-step approach and learning from lower-level observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid building constitutions from abstract metaphysics, geometry, or arithmetic alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutional design must reference moral and political realities; relying solely on metaphysical/ geometric/arithmetic schemes is fallacious and produces impractical or unjust systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "It is remarkable...not one reference whatsoever is to be found to anything moral or anything politic...Hominem non sapiunt." Example: dividing territory into equal geometric squares or giving exact arithmetical voting shares without regard for human relations leads to absurdities and local inconveniences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat rhetorical paradoxes or literary devices as literal policy foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradoxes used in literature or rhetoric as means to astonish should not be taken up as serious grounds of action by legislators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: copying satirists' or rhetoricians' paradoxes into policy. "These paradoxes become with them serious grounds of action...If this was true of Cato, these gentlemen copy after him..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral qualifications must not subvert proclaimed equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications for voting or office (e.g., property or tax-payments thresholds) that contradict the professed natural equality of citizens are unjust and destroy rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: primary assembly qualification of 'local valuation of three days' labor', election eligibility of 'ten days' labor' or paying 'a mark of silver' — all these impose barriers that exclude the poorest and establish a tyrannous aristocracy contrary to equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation bases must be coherent with the principle they claim to embody
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing bases of representation (territory, population, contribution), the method must consistently reflect the underlying principle and not produce contradictory or self-defeating outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burke critiques the Assembly's threefold bases (territory/geometry; population/arithmetic; contribution/finance) as held together incoherently — e.g., giving an arbitrary 'third' to geometry without justification, or combining conflicting bases so they produce absurd inequalities between masses.

rubrics_metrics.name: If using contribution as a basis, measure actual contributors not territorial proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation 'according to contribution' must identify who actually contributes (direct vs indirect contributions) rather than simply assigning credit to territorial masses, because consumption and revenues cross territorial lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The indirect contribution...is in truth a better standard...The consumers of commodities imported into Bordeaux, who are scattered through all France, pay the import duties of Bordeaux." Failure to account for this leads to inequitable local preferences and misapportioned representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating aristocratic masses that betray their stated democratic principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemes that attempt to protect wealth by creating larger corporate representation for wealthy districts (rather than protecting rich individuals or a distinct class) produce perverse and ineffective protections and increase risks to the wealthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burke shows how giving a district more deputies ostensibly to protect the rich actually creates more democratic posts that can be used by ambitious poor to undermine wealthy individuals; if protection was intended, it should be conferred on rich individuals or a class, not a territorial mass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure national coherence and subordination among local bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative subdivisions (cantons, communes, departments) should be designed to maintain connection, coherence, and disciplined subordination; severing the country into largely independent republics undermines unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "You cannot but perceive...it has a direct and immediate tendency to sever France into a variety of republics...render them totally independent of each other, without any direct constitutional means of coherence, connection, or subordination." Anti-pattern: producing many self-contained bodies with no coordinating constitutional mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect historical/local institutions, manners, and social ties when reforming
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating a country as if conquered — destroying vestiges of religion, polity, laws, and manners — damages the social fabric and undermines durable government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "They have imitated the policy of the harshest of that harsh race...to destroy all vestiges of the ancient country..." Advises against wholesale cultural/political erasure in name of reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware that mechanically equal geometrical/arithmetical schemes produce inequity in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal equality of measurement (equal squares, equal head-counts) does not guarantee substantive equality of representation or power because social, economic, and historical factors vary widely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed examples comparing cantons with differing populations and contributions show how geometric/arithmetical allocations can create striking and unjust inequalities (e.g., a wealthy trading canton sending ten deputies vs two poorer cantons sending six).
